theme.title: NBA Mix 41
theme.subtitle: Five moments from across NBA history
theme.recap: Five NBA stories, five different numbers: a quick tour of stars, teams, records and surprises.

questions.prompt: How long was the Miami Heat's 2012–13 winning streak?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Heat embarked on a 27-game winning streak

funFacts.text: The winning run began with a Super Bowl Sunday victory over Toronto and eventually became a franchise record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat defeated the Toronto Raptors on Super Bowl Sunday to start what would become the longest winning streak

funFacts.text: Miami rallied from a huge third-quarter deficit in Cleveland during the run, then won the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat overcame a league high 27-point third-quarter deficit to defeat the Cleveland Cavaliers

funFacts.text: Chicago finally stopped Miami's historic run in late March, although the Heat would still secure the top East seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat fall 101–97 to the Chicago Bulls, ending their winning streak

questions.prompt: How many threes did Stephen Curry make in Game 2 of the 2018 Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: set an NBA Finals record in Game 2 with nine three-point field goals

funFacts.text: Golden State increased its defensive double-teaming of LeBron after his enormous opening performance.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors employed more double teams against James in Game 2

funFacts.text: J. R. Smith struggled from the floor, with both of his field goals coming early in the night.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Smith struggled for Cleveland, shooting 2-for-9 (22.2%) with both baskets coming in the first quarter

funFacts.text: Kevin Durant contributed rebounds and playmaking alongside Curry, making Golden State's offense tougher to stop.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Warriors got 26 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists from Kevin Durant

questions.prompt: How many rebounds per game did Shawn Kemp average for the Sonics?
questions.note: 10.8 rebounds per game as one of the West's top forwards.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Shawn Kemp averaged 18.1 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 2.1 blocks per game

funFacts.text: Kemp also averaged 2.1 blocks per game that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 10.8 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 2.1 blocks per game

funFacts.text: He earned All-NBA Second Team honors alongside Seattle's regular-season rise.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: and was named to the All-NBA Second Team

funFacts.text: Kemp competed in the Slam Dunk Contest for the fourth time in his career.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Kemp also participated in the NBA Slam Dunk Contest for the fourth time

questions.prompt: The 1999–2000 Pacers set a franchise record for consecutive home wins. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including a franchise-best 25 game win streak at home

funFacts.text: The Pacers finally defeated the rival Knicks in the Eastern finals to reach their first NBA championship series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Pacers advanced to the NBA Finals for the first time in franchise history

funFacts.text: Indiana's coach during that Finals run was former Boston Celtics star Larry Bird.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Indiana Pacers  Larry Bird

funFacts.text: Both finalists were playing in newly opened home arenas, Indiana's Fieldhouse and Los Angeles's Staples Center.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: both teams in the Finals featured newly built arenas

questions.prompt: Reserve Leon Powe played only 15 minutes in Game 2 of the 2008 Finals. How many points did he score?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Leon Powe scored 21 points on 6–7 shooting from the field and 9–13 from the line in 15 minutes of play

funFacts.text: Powe's physical first stint drew ten free-throw attempts almost immediately.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: drew ten free-throw attempts within his first three minutes on the court

funFacts.text: His consecutive thunderous dunks had the home crowd chanting his name.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: back-to-back dunks in the last minute of the 3rd quarter, causing the Boston crowd to chant his name

funFacts.text: Powe alone attempted more free throws than the entire Lakers roster in Game 2.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Over the course of the game, Powe shot 13 free throws while the Lakers shot 10
